institution: Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, New Delhi
citation: Department of Clinical Microbiology and Immunology, Sir Ganga Ram Hospital. Microbiology Newsletter, Vol. 19, No. 2: % sensitivity in yeasts fungi (blood isolates), January to December 2012. New Delhi: Sir Ganga Ram Hospital; published October 2013.
reporting: Percent susceptible of yeasts isolated from blood, by species, for the whole hospital (one table, not split by OPD, ward and ICU), with the number of isolates tested per species in parentheses; amphotericin B, flucytosine, fluconazole, voriconazole and caspofungin; a second table re-interprets three species with CLSI M27-S4.
method: Vitek 2 YST antifungal susceptibility cards (bioMerieux, France) and E test, repeat isolates excluded; cumulative antibiogram per CLSI M39-A (printed "CLSI M-39A Vol. 22, No. 8; 2002 (global consensus guidelines)"); interpreted as per CLSI M27-A3 (the recorded table; a second table re-interprets three species per CLSI M27-S4, December 2012); amphotericin B is reported as the percentage of isolates with MIC <1 µg/ml.

verification.note: The page 2 table was parsed from the PDF text layer (pdfplumber word positions; each cell assigned to its drug column by x position, the species label and the number tested read from the label), then every cell and every n was compared by eye with page 2 rendered at scale 4, first as the whole table band and then each of the two narrow tables cropped on its own: no differences. Both tables on the page (the main CLSI M27-A3 table and the three-row CLSI M27-S4 table) were parsed and compared. Footnote marks and every cell printed with a symbol or text (NA, SDD, "-") were read on the image. The other content (charts, filamentous fungi table and antifungal use chart on pages 2 and 3; pages 1 and 4 to 8) was identified from the text layer and the rendered pages only to describe it in excluded. A second reader re-read every cell and n against the page images on 2026-09-26 (see issues).

notes: Microbiology Newsletter of Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, Vol. 19, No. 2 (published October 2013), data January to December 2012, 8 pages. The No. 2 issue of each year carries the mycology, mycobacteriology, virology and serology results (the bacterial antibiogram is in No. 1). Recorded: the page 2 table "% Sensitivity in Yeasts Fungi* (Blood Isolates 2012)", one row per species with the number of isolates tested printed in parentheses (used as n, n_tested) and percent susceptible for amphotericin B, flucytosine, fluconazole, voriconazole and caspofungin. The table covers blood isolates of all locations together and is not split by OPD, ward and ICU, so every row is set "all". Footnotes: "- = Not done"; "Antifungal susceptibility results have been interpreted as per CLSI M27A3 document"; the * and ** footnotes as in the 2011 edition (Vitek 2 YST cards, E test, repeat isolates excluded, CLSI M39-A 2002; amphotericin B as isolates with MIC <1 µg/ml, noted on every amphotericin B cell). A second, smaller table on the right, "Antifungal Susceptibility Results Interpreted as per CLSI M27S4 Document (Dec 2012)", re-interprets C. tropicalis, C. albicans and C. parapsilosis with the newer breakpoints; the main table is recorded because it covers all 14 species with one standard, and the M27-S4 figures are kept in excluded. Organism names: "C. guillermondi" is recorded as Candida guilliermondii and "Kodamea ohmeri" as Kodamaea ohmeri. Species without an organism key are listed in excluded with their printed figures: "C. haemulonii (23)", "C. rugosa (3)". The paragraph under the table gives the blood cases and share of each species, which can differ from the numbers tested; organism counts from the charts are not recorded (see excluded). The PDF has no direct link: sgrh.com serves the newsletters only by an HTTP POST from the Microbiology Newsletter issue selector on https://sgrh.com/en/publications. This issue (Vol. 19, No. 2, October 2013) is not listed in the selector at all; it was obtained by POSTing microbiology=October-2013 to the same form. The fungal issues are recorded as their own series (Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, fungal), so their editions trend with each other and are not taken for editions of the bacterial antibiogram published in the first issue of each volume.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: every cell and every row n re-read from page 2 rendered at scale 4 (the table cut into two halves with the species column kept on both, footnotes cropped separately) and written down before comparing with the file; the seeded sample from sample_cells.py is part of this. All 59 cells and 12 n of the recorded CLSI M27-A3 main table, plus the 10 figures of its 2 excluded rows (C. haemulonii 23, C. rugosa 3) and all 15 figures of the three-row CLSI M27-S4 inset on the right: 0 transcription errors, nothing corrected.

Confirmed: the main table (14 species, footnote "interpreted as per CLSI M27A3 document") is the right one to record and breakpoints "CLSI M27-A3" matches the page; the M27-S4 inset (C. tropicalis 40, C. albicans 33, C. parapsilosis 32) is correctly excluded with its figures and the differences listed. Trichosporon spp. flucytosine "-" (legend "- = Not done") left out with the right note. The intrinsic cell C. krusei fluconazole 0 is printed that way (not a transcription error).
